skill.name: web-research
skill.description: A prompt-only skill for planning web research, gathering information with available search tools, and synthesizing cited findings.
skill.summary: Plan, gather, and synthesize web research with clear sources.
skill.author: DougTrajano

security_audit.summary: No static security findings were reported for this prompt-only skill. Review of SKILL.md found a benign research workflow and no prompt injection, executable code, network exfiltration, or credential handling instructions.

content.user_title: Research the Web with a Structured Method
content.value_statement: Web research can become unfocused when questions span many sources. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through planning, searching, and cited synthesis.
actual_capabilities: Breaks a research question into focused subtopics before searching.
Recommends a bounded search approach for each subtopic.
Guides collection and organization of findings from available web tools.
Supports comparative analysis across multiple subjects.
Prompts the agent to synthesize answers with source URLs and limitations.
limitations: It does not include executable scripts, APIs, or bundled search tools.
It depends on the host agent's web access and citation capabilities.
It does not automatically verify source authority or factual accuracy.
It is designed for research workflows, not private investigation or surveillance.

use_cases.title: Market Landscape Scan
use_cases.description: Research a product category, organize key players, and summarize current public information with source links.

use_cases.title: Policy or Standards Brief
use_cases.description: Gather current public guidance from official sources and synthesize practical implications for a team.

use_cases.title: Competitive Feature Comparison
use_cases.description: Compare several tools or vendors using focused searches for pricing, features, documentation, and recent announcements.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Topic Research
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you need a concise researched answer.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the web-research skill to research [topic]. Create a short plan, run focused searches, and return a cited summary with any gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when evaluating two or three alternatives.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the web-research skill to compare [option A], [option B], and [option C]. Search each option separately, then synthesize strengths, weaknesses, and source-backed differences.

prompt_templates.title: Current State Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the web-research skill to produce a current brief on [topic]. Prioritize official and recent sources, cite URLs, and separate confirmed facts from uncertain claims.

prompt_templates.title: Research Report with Gaps
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a deeper investigation with explicit limits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the web-research skill to investigate [research question]. Define 3 to 5 subtopics, limit searches per subtopic, synthesize findings, and list unresolved questions.

output_examples.input: Research current options for enterprise passwordless authentication.
output: A short research plan with subtopics such as vendors, standards, deployment models, and risks.
A synthesized summary that cites source URLs and identifies areas needing further verification.

output_examples.input: Compare three project management tools for a small engineering team.
output: A comparison organized by pricing, integrations, roadmap tracking, reporting, and source availability.
A final recommendation section that explains tradeoffs and notes missing information.

output_examples.input: Prepare a brief on recent public guidance for AI governance.
output: A cited brief using official or primary sources where possible.
A limitations section that separates dated guidance, draft proposals, and active rules.

best_practices: Start with a clear research question and 2 to 5 non-overlapping subtopics.
Prefer primary or official sources when accuracy and recency matter.
End with cited synthesis, known gaps, and practical next steps.
anti_patterns: Do not search broadly without first defining subtopics and expected evidence.
Do not treat uncited claims as verified facts.
Do not continue searching after enough reliable evidence answers the question.

faq.question: Does this skill browse the web by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides a research workflow and relies on the agent's available web search tools.

faq.question: Can it produce cited reports?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow instructs the agent to include source URLs in the final synthesis.

faq.question: Is this skill useful for recent topics?
faq.answer: Yes, when the host agent has current web access. The skill encourages focused searches and source checks.

faq.question: How many searches should it run?
faq.answer: The skill recommends 3 to 5 searches per subtopic, depending on complexity.

faq.question: Does it include executable code?
faq.answer: No. It is a prompt-only methodology file with no scripts or bundled tools.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
